==English==
{{wp}}
[[Image:Steam denver market street.jpg|right|thumb|Steam rising from the street grates. (vapor condensing into mist)]]

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|steem}}, {{m|enm|stem}}, from {{inh|en|ang|stēam||steam, hot exhalation, hot breath; that which emits vapour; blood}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*staumaz||steam, vapour, breath}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dʰewh₂-||to whirl, waft, stink, shake; steam, haze, smoke}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|stem}}, {{m|sco|steam||steam}}, {{cog|fy|steam||steam, vapour}}, {{cog|nl|stoom||steam, vapour}}, {{cog|nds|stom||steam}}, {{cog|sv|-}} dialectal {{m|sv|stimma||steam, fog}}, {{cog|la|fūmus||smoke, steam}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|stēm}}, {{IPA|en|/stiːm/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/stiːm/|a=GA}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-steam.ogg|a=GA}}
* {{rhymes|en|iːm|s=1}}

===Noun===
{{wikidata lexeme|L4608}}
{{en-noun|-|s}}

# {{senseid|en|Q3251738}} The hot [[gaseous]] form of [[water]], formed when water changes from the [[liquid]] [[phase]] to the [[gas]] [[phase]] (at or above its [[boiling point]] temperature).
#: {{hyper|en|water vapor<id:Q190120><qq:sometimes construed as coordinate><!--when sub-BP water vapor is meant implicitly-->|<|water#Noun|<|compound#Noun|;|substance#Noun}}
# The suspended condensate ({{l|en|cloud}}) formed by water vapour when it encounters colder air.
## {{l|en|mist|Mist}}, {{l|en|fog}}.
## Exhaled breath into cold air below the dew point of the exhalation.
# [[pressurized|Pressurized]] water vapour used for [[heating]], [[cooking]], or to [[provide]] [[mechanical]] [[energy]].
# The act of [[cook]]ing by [[#Verb|steam]]ing.
#: {{ux|en|Give the carrots a ten-minute '''steam'''.}}
# {{lb|en|figuratively}} Internal [[energy]] for [[progress]] or [[motive]] [[power]].
#: {{syn|en|stamina}}
#: {{ux|en|After three weeks in bed he was finally able to sit up under his own '''steam'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|[[run out of steam|run out of '''steam''']]}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1927|author=Irvin Shrewsbury Cobb|title=Ladies and Gentlemen|page=129
|passage=Them that puts the most '''steam''' into it will get a [[finnuf]] slipped to 'em.}}
# {{lb|en|figuratively}} [[pent-up|Pent-up]] [[anger]].
#: {{ux|en|Dad had to go outside to [[blow off steam|blow off some '''steam''']].}}
# A steam-powered vehicle, referring to their use.
# Travel by means of a steam-powered vehicle. {{rfex|en}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} Any [[exhalation]].
#* {{RQ:Milton Comus|passage=a '''steam''' of rich, distilled perfumes}}
# {{lb|en|fencing}} [[fencing|Fencing]] without the use of any electric equipment.

===Verb===
{{wikidata lexeme|L28016}}
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive|cooking}} To [[cook]] with [[#Noun|steam]].
#: {{ux|en|The best way to cook artichokes is to '''steam''' them.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|literal|figurative}} To be cooked with steam.
#: {{ux|en|The artichokes are '''steaming''' in the pot.}}
#: {{ux|en|I'm '''steaming''' in this coat.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To expose to the action of [[#Noun|steam]]; to apply steam to for softening, dressing, or preparing.
#: {{ux|en|to '''steam''' wood or cloth}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[raise]] steam, e.g. in a [[steam locomotive]].
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[produce]] or [[vent]] [[#Noun|steam]].
#* {{RQ:Dryden Indian Emperour|page=36|passage=See, ſee, my Brother's Ghoſt hangs hovering there, / O're his vvarm Blood, that '''ſteems''' into the Air, / Revenge, Revenge it cries.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To rise in vapour; to issue, or pass off, as vapour.
#: {{ux|en|Our breath '''steamed''' in the cold winter air.}}
#* {{RQ:Boyle Physiological Essays|page=66|passage=[T]he diſſolved Amber vvas plainly diſcernable ſvvimming like a thin film upon the ſurface of the Liquor, vvhence little by little it '''ſteamed''' avvay into the air.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|figuratively}} To become [[angry]]; to [[fume]]; to be [[incensed]].
# {{lb|en|transitive|figuratively}} To make [[angry]].
#: {{ux|en|It really '''steams''' me to see her treat him like that.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[cover]] with [[condensed]] [[water vapor]].
#: {{ux|en|With all the heavy breathing going on the windows were quickly '''steamed''' in the car.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[travel]] by means of [[steam power]].
#: {{ux|en|We '''steamed''' around the Mediterranean.}}
#: {{ux|en|The ship '''steamed''' out of the harbour.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1913|author={{w|Edgar Rice Burroughs}}|title={{w|The Return of Tarzan}}|publisher=Ballantine Books|location=New York|year_published=1963|page=112|passage=“Yes, Tennington, of course,” ventured Clayton; “it must be a bully idea if you had it, but what the deuce is it? Goin’ to '''steam''' to China via the south pole?”}}
# {{lb|en|figuratively|or|literally}} To [[move]] with great or excessive [[purposefulness]].
#: {{ux|en|If he heard of anyone picking the fruit he would '''steam''' off and lecture them.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=16 Dec 90|volume=18|number=22|journal=Gay Community News|page=6|author=Chris Nealon|title=Washhington Paper Celebrates Les/Gay Unions|text=The No on 35 drive garnered the support of Black, Asian, and progressive church communities, and '''steamed''' to victory with 58 percent of the vote on Nov. 6.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To [[exhale]].
#* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=III|canto=I|passage=like inward fire that outward smoke had '''steemd''' }}
